scope_reviewed: crates/axc-hir/src/typecheck.rs (ISSUE-1 Assign routing, both FLAT and NESTED arms)
positive_feedback: OpPhi emission follows the §A.4 10-step sequence exactly: pre-header values captured before OpBranch closes the block; header_block_idx captured immediately after begin_block(header); phi_ids installed in var_ids BEFORE body emission so body reads resolve to the phi (not the stale pre-header value); latch_values captured after body emission via the SSA-rebind path; phi instructions post-inserted at InsertPoint::Begin in REVERSE order so they land in declaration order; select_block(merge_idx) restores the selected block; var_ids[B] left = phi_id on exit so post-loop stores read the merged value (zero-trip safe). Mechanically airtight.

ISSUE-2 (Assign SSA-rebind) is cleanly symmetric to the existing Let coopmat branch: `if coopmat_binding_ids.contains(binding) { var_ids.insert(*binding, val_id) } else { b.store(...) }`. The distinction is architecturally correct — coopmat values are opaque tensors that cannot live in Function-class OpVariable storage.

ISSUE-1 (typecheck routing) is correctly applied to BOTH the FLAT Assign arm (typecheck.rs:~1057, for out-of-loop reassigns) and the NESTED Assign arm (typecheck.rs:~1656, for in-loop reassigns). Both arms now branch on BindingTy::CoopMatrix and route through check_coopmat_init_expr, giving use_==Accumulator + full shape validation for free from the existing function — no new error variant needed.

AT-1707 is genuinely load-bearing: the opphi_coopmat_accumulate.axc kernel loads A and B directly from global buffers (no shared staging), accumulates K_ITER=4 times, and asserts max_diff==0 vs K_ITER*(A·B). If OpPhi emission were broken (phi operands swapped, latch not updated, wrong predecessor labels), the GPU output would be A·B (a single iteration) rather than 4*A·B, and max_diff > 0. This is a real falsifiable test, not a compile-only anchor. QA confirmed GPU PASS on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000.

AT-1700 is a solid non-regression guard: the scalar reduction.axc kernel asserts exactly 0 OpPhi in the binary. This protects the Function-storage path from being accidentally touched — scalars must never get header phis.

AT-1701 validates SPIR-V structural correctness of the phi: 1 phi in the loop header, 7 words (3 fixed + 2 predecessor pairs), both predecessor labels valid OpLabel result_ids in the module. The raw binary scanner is clean and extension-agnostic (rspirv dr::Loader cannot parse cooperative-matrix opcodes).

AT-1704 (a/b/c/d) is thorough: (a) break over coopmat-carrying loop → hard error, (b) continue → hard error, (c) scalar break still compiles, (d) inner loop break not rejected by outer coopmat guard. The non-descend discipline (break/continue scan does not recurse into nested ForRange/While) is correctly implemented and tested.

The honest deferral is clean in all four dimensions: (1) AT-1620/1622 GPU tests are empty #[ignore] stubs with an honest eprintln explaining the N>tile_n coverage gap — not quarantined-but-claiming-pass; (2) resident_matmul_competitive.rs was removed and its bench Cargo.toml entry does not exist; (3) no competitive TFLOPS number is reported; (4) DESIGN.md §3.1.15 PART B and ROADMAP.md both accurately describe AT-1620/1622 as compile+spirv-val-only WIP. The post-QA honesty fix (commit 802debf) resolved the false 'bit-exact' claims QA flagged.

The AT-1702 structural assertion (added in commit 802debf) now verifies that each nested loop header has exactly 1 phi with exactly 2 predecessor pairs (7-word instruction). The comment explicitly justifies that the full outer-phi-latch-operand == inner-phi-result-id walk is delegated to AT-1707's end-to-end GPU proof. This is a defensible engineering trade-off given AT-1707's bit-exact assertion would catch the composition failure.

matmul_shared_f32.axc index-math fix is clear and correctly diagnosed: global_row = gid(1), tile_row = global_row/16, local_row = global_row - tile_row*16. The original bug (both tile_row and local_row reading gid(1)) caused a_global_row = gid(1)*16 + gid(1) (rows 0,17,34...) on multi-workgroup dispatches. The comment explains the fix precisely.

tiled_attention.axc dispatch-geometry fix is minimal and correct: the kernel source was already correct (q_row = gid(0)), the bug was that the host dispatched (1,1,1) instead of (seq_len,1,1). The AT-1630 test uses the matching CPU reference with IDENTICAL Taylor exp (1+x+x²/2), avoiding any exp-precision disagreement.

Public API is additive: two new BodyCodegenError variants (LoopCarriedCoopMatAcrossBreakUnsupported / LoopCarriedCoopMatAcrossContinueUnsupported) and detect_loop_carried_coopmat (private), stmt_reassigns_binding (private). No existing error variants removed. Typecheck routing is additive branching only.

The two .expect() calls in detect_loop_carried_coopmat are invariant guards on conditions guaranteed by construction (binding is in coopmat_binding_ids iff it was inserted there during Let emission, so it always has a var_ids entry by the time it reaches detect). The pattern is consistent with existing codebase usage. No .unwrap() or .expect() added in any public-facing codepath.

minor_issues.description: AT-1702 asserts each nested phi has exactly 2 predecessor pairs (7 words) and distinct result IDs, but does NOT walk phi[5] (outer latch operand id) to assert it equals the inner phi's result id (phi_result_ids[1]). The spec §A.7 called this out as the composition-correctness assertion. The 7-word check would only catch a wrong number of predecessors, not a stale pre-inner id that happens to produce a valid 7-word phi.
minor_issues.justification_for_non_blocking: AT-1707 is the end-to-end GPU proof: if the outer loop's latch operand were a stale pre-inner id rather than the inner phi's result, the K_ITER-accumulation would produce a wrong value and AT-1707 would FAIL (max_diff != 0). The binary composition invariant is therefore indirectly enforced. Flagging for follow-up only.
minor_issues.suggested_fix: In a follow-up, extend AT-1702 to: `assert_eq!(outer_phi_latch_val_id, phi_result_ids[1], 'AT-1702: outer phi latch operand must be the inner phi result id')` by reading headers[0].1[0][5] (the outer phi's latch value word).

minor_issues.description: The type lookup for phi emission walks all function blocks to find the instruction with result_id == pre_header_val_id. This is O(instructions) per phi per loop, which is fine for today's kernels, but the comment could note that a coopmat_type_cache keyed by BindingId already exists (used elsewhere in body.rs) and could be used directly here to avoid the module walk entirely.
minor_issues.justification_for_non_blocking: Correctness is unaffected. The walk is bounded by module size and only executed for loop-carried coopmat bindings (rare in practice). Performance of the compiler at today's kernel sizes is negligible.

minor_issues.description: The file header references the N>tile_n limitation but does not name the upcoming follow-up milestone (e.g. 'M3.x multi-N-tile output loop'). A one-line TODO cross-reference would help future agents find the deferred work.
minor_issues.justification_for_non_blocking: ROADMAP.md already tracks this; no functional impact.

ISSUE-1 (typecheck Assign routing) and ISSUE-2 (body.rs Assign SSA-rebind) are cleanly fixed in both FLAT and NESTED arms. AT-1707 is a genuine GPU proof that would falsify a broken OpPhi. AT-1621 (f32 matmul bit-exact) and AT-1630 (attention within-1e-3) are real GPU-proven assertions. Scalar path is unchanged (AT-1700 guards this).
